title: Compliance crosswalk: Hazira gas release and fire, 2020
audience: HSE leads, management-system owners and auditors
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person.

bottom_line.text: The register gives partial evidence for 17 of 23 ISO 45001 clauses and 16 of the 20 RBPS elements; no requirement is evidenced here outright, because no learning carries clause ids yet. Emergency preparedness (8.2, nine learnings), operational control (8.1) and internal audit (9.2, eight each) draw on the most.

The organisation must still show its own evidence for 6 ISO 45001 clauses (among them 5.4 worker consultation, 7.3 awareness and 9.3 management review) and 4 RBPS elements (among them workforce involvement and management review). The nearest learnings, on overdue audit actions and drill records without actions, are a lead for those rows, not that evidence.
The learnings speak most directly to change management, emergency isolation, competence for emergency duty and audits that recorded compliance without site data.

items.text: Aid to assurance, not a compliance opinion.

sections.heading: What the learnings show, requirement by requirement

items.lesson: Changes of part and material went ahead without a change review, because the change procedure was never triggered.
items.explanation: RBPS management of change and ISO 45001 clause 8.1 (operational planning and control): LR-06 shows the procedure existed on paper but had not been used since 2018, so a like-for-unlike replacement was not seen as a change. The organisation must still show its own change records and how a replacement part triggers a review.

items.lesson: Pressure-boundary work returned to service tested only at operating pressure, because no procedure defined the test.
items.explanation: RBPS operating procedures: LR-02 shows that no procedure required a test to design pressure before return to service. The organisation must still show the return-to-service procedures it holds for high-pressure joints and how they are kept current.

items.lesson: The thickness inspection cycle slipped from four years to six, with no escalation and no baseline data.
items.explanation: RBPS asset integrity and reliability: LR-18 shows an inspection schedule that could slip without escalation, and missing baseline data and pipe schedules. The organisation must still show its inspection plan, how overdue inspections are escalated, and the baseline records it now holds.

items.lesson: Measured pipe-wall loss was recorded but not turned into a corrective plan for three years.
items.explanation: ISO 45001 clause 10.2 (incident, nonconformity and corrective action): LR-17 shows that inspection results were recorded but no role owned acting on them, and painting stood in for the fix. The organisation must still show how a measured nonconformity becomes a corrective action with a review of its effectiveness.

items.lesson: The emergency plan named the major-leak scenario but gave no isolation criteria and no delegated authority to isolate.
items.explanation: RBPS emergency management and ISO 45001 clause 8.2 (emergency preparedness and response): LR-07 shows that people at the scene had no criteria and no authority to isolate a major supply. The organisation must still show its emergency plans, the isolation criteria they now set and who holds the authority.

items.lesson: Control-room staff held emergency duties after a general course, with no defined qualification or simulator practice.
items.explanation: RBPS training and performance assurance and ISO 45001 clause 7.2 (competence): LR-12 shows that no qualification was defined for control-room emergency duty. The organisation must still show the competence requirements for each emergency role and the records of who meets them.

items.lesson: The metering drawing in use was an unapproved vendor drawing that did not match the field.
items.explanation: RBPS process knowledge management: LR-19 shows a lost original drawing replaced by one nobody had approved or checked against the plant. The organisation must still show how it keeps as-built drawings true and who approves vendor drawings.

items.lesson: Maintenance notifications stood in for work permits, permits went missing untracked, and job safety plans were absent.
items.explanation: RBPS safe work practices: LR-22 shows a permit system that let a notification replace a permit and did not track missing permits. The organisation must still show its permit records and how it tracks that every hazardous job had a permit and a task-specific hazard review.

items.lesson: Safety audits used generic checklists and recorded compliance without site data, so they could not find plant-specific defects.
items.explanation: RBPS auditing and ISO 45001 clause 9.2 (internal audit): LR-20 shows audits that could report compliance without anyone having looked at the plant. The organisation must still show its audit programme, the completed checklists and the site data behind each audit result.

items.lesson: People saw the release first, but their warnings reached the control room late and diluted.
items.explanation: ISO 45001 clause 7.4 (communication): LR-13 shows that perimeter and security staff had no direct line to the control room and no standard words for a release. The organisation must still show its internal communication arrangements for an emergency warning.

sections.heading: Requirements not checked against the primary text

items.text: 15 of the 23 ISO 45001 rows and 16 of the 20 RBPS rows carry "(unverified)": their ids and titles were not checked against the primary text of the standard. Confirm them against the current edition before using the crosswalk in an audit.
